correctness.rationale: The four-world models have nonempty neighborhoods. Convexity follows from an antichain in the first family and a single covering inclusion in the second. The type-support induction handles atoms, falsum, conjunction, inquisitive disjunction, implication, and arbitrarily nested unary existential/universal neighborhood operators. Each unary operator reduces respectively to the same minimal or maximal valuation-type neighborhood in both models; the fixed binary conditional differs via the inserted middle-profile neighborhood. The packaged checker tests convexity, 19 exhaustive downward-closed 3-type predicates, 38 unary quantifier comparisons, 5776 implication state comparisons, and the conditional. A separate deterministic direct semantics test checks 2500 formulas at all 16 states in both models. Computation does not replace the infinite syntactic induction.

originality.rationale: Ciardelli (arXiv:2411.04031, Open Problem 4.6) explicitly asks whether the binary conditional is definable from both unary modalities on convex models. The established unrestricted-frame nondefinability and existential-only upward-monotone result do not imply the convex restricted claim, because restriction can restore definability and adding the universal modality expands expressive resources. Checked adjacent primary works concern convex team-support properties or one-world classical bundled operators, neither of which implies this separation. Searches of indexed findings for direct equivalences, parameter variants and aliases found no dominating result. This supports best-knowledge priority but not uniqueness; possible unindexed solutions are recorded as risks.
residual_risks: An equivalent answer to Open Problem 4.6 may exist in unindexed or subsequently circulated literature; database silence is not priority certification.
Adjacent primary papers were examined at the relevant semantic and main-result sections, not claimed to be searched exhaustively for every theorem in all appendices.

value.rationale: The theorem directly answers a stated research question on restricted-model expressivity, a structural issue unresolved by unrestricted-model separation. Its two explicitly convex frames isolate the reason for failure: the unary modalities observe only extremal propositional-type profiles under homogeneous valuations, while the conditional detects an intermediate support pattern. The result is not just a computational census or an arbitrary small counterexample; it supplies an unrestricted-depth induction transferable to related modal-fragment comparisons.
